extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans to evaluate Large Vision-Language Models' (LVLMs) multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from current benchmarks (MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, MathVista) with an automated pipeline using LLMs as inspectors to filter for visual dependency and data leakage. Subsequently, three experts conducted manual review to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements. Samples were split into four difficulty levels based on LVLM hit counts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing multi-modal benchmarks including MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were filtered using an automated pipeline with 8 LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) to exclude samples answerable by more than 2 LLMs. Remaining samples were evaluated by 16 LVLMs to gauge difficulty and split into four levels (easy, moderate, hard, tough).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline filtered samples from a pool of 22,401 down to 11,607 candidates by checking if they could be answered by LLMs without visual input. A manual review process by three experts further curated 1,500 high-quality samples ensuring visual dependency and minimal data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of multiple-choice questions with images. Annotations (correct answers) were derived from existing benchmarks. The curation process involved human experts reviewing samples to ensure they met criteria for visual dependency and minimal data leakage, rather than creating new labels from scratch.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three experts conducted the manual review process.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, IntemLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B, GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series, ShareGPT4V, Monkey-Chat, CogVLM-Chat, Yi-VL, IntemVL-Chat-v1.2, Sphinx-X-MoE
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to provide a more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of LVLMs by addressing issues of unnecessary visual content and data leakage in existing benchmarks, which can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains and misguide research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset addresses biases in existing benchmarks where answers could be inferred from text alone or due to data leakage. It aims to reduce these biases by curating vision-indispensable samples.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains 1,500 samples. It is designed to evaluate multi-modal capabilities but may not cover all possible domains or edge cases. The authors note that future work plans to expand it into a larger, online test set.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Specifically used for evaluating the multi-modal capabilities of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) and measuring multi-modal gain and leakage.
